articles.title: Pay for the power, not for the design
articles.subtitle: A closer look at value for money in this category
articles.excerpt: Apple Watch review: Design. For a slightly more opinionated version of the video review above, here's the male half of the team arguing...
articles.author: ashraf

content.text: When it comes to buying a new laptop, the temptation is always to chase the sleekest design on the shelf. But for anyone doing real work — video editing, development, heavy multitasking — raw power should come before polish.

We benchmarked a range of machines at similar price points and found that the best-looking laptops were rarely the best performing. The extra budget going into unibody machining and slimmer bezels often comes directly out of the thermal and battery budget.

items: Sustained performance under load, not just peak benchmarks
Upgradeable RAM and storage where possible
Keyboard and trackpad quality for daily use
Battery life under real workloads, not marketing claims

content.text: Our recommendation: shortlist by specs first, then let design be the tiebreaker between machines that already meet your performance bar.
